metadata.description: Omelette's design setup: the outside design plugins it uses, each pinned to a commit that was read and checked.

plugins.name: frontend-design
plugins.description: Anthropic's frontend-design skill: commits to an aesthetic direction and a real type pairing before any code, so the result does not fall back to the average look.

plugins.name: impeccable
plugins.description: Paul Bakaus's Impeccable 4.8.2: commands you run on a narrow target (critique, audit, polish, bolder, quieter, typeset, layout, animate and more), a detector with 62 rules and no model behind it, and a hook that leaves notes after UI edits and never blocks. Its engine binary downloads on first use and is checked against pinned checksums. Keep its live mode off: it can start claude with permissions bypassed.

plugins.name: modern-web-guidance
plugins.description: Google Chrome's guides to what the web platform now does natively (dialogs, styled selects, anchor positioning, view transitions). Measured by its authors at +27 to +34 points on their task suite.

plugins.name: emil-design-engineering
plugins.description: Emil Kowalski's design-engineering skills: animate, review-animations, break-ui (worst-case data), prototype (variants behind a picker), mobile-native. The repo's whole skills folder loads, including a few platform skills (Expo, Swift).

plugins.name: stageshow
plugins.description: Benji Taylor's Stageshow (MIT): faux product UI, as stills or short animations, built against gold examples and filmed frame by frame to catch one-frame jumps and text that does not fit. For case-study stills and films and product heroes. Filming needs playwright-core in the project and Chrome, or CHROME_PATH set to another Chromium (Brave).
